label: Challenge: Barnard's Star (fastest-moving star)
note: Its 2026 position: it has moved about 4.5′ north since 2000. It moves about 10″ a year, under 2 pixels, so zoom right in and press ▶: compare the Aug 2025 visits with Aug 2026.

label: Challenge: Epsilon Indi B (brown dwarf pair)
note: Two brown dwarfs orbiting the star Epsilon Indi, which is about 7′ away. They move about 4.7″ a year. Cold objects: tick Long colours, zoom in, press ▶.

label: Challenge: WISE 0855 (coldest known brown dwarf)
note: Its 2026 position: about 2′ west of the coordinates in the challenge, because it moves about 8″ a year. It is almost invisible below 4 µm: tick Long colours, zoom in, press ▶.

label: Challenge: RW Aurigae (variable young star)
note: A young star that brightens and fades irregularly. 33 visits from Sep 2025 to Sep 2026: click the star to see its brightness over time.

label: Challenge: R Draconis (pulsating Mira star)
note: A red giant that swells and shrinks every ~245 days. SPHEREx visited 205 times in 17 months (it sits near the deep field): click the star to see it brighten and fade.

label: Andromeda Galaxy (M31), wide view
note: Our nearest big galaxy, 2.5 million light-years away. Zoom in, then press ▶ Play over time.

label: Asteroid Abundantia racing across (Jan 2026)
note: A bright main-belt asteroid crosses this field in about 10 hours. Press play on the Jan 2026 visit.

label: Asteroid Menzel on the move (Jan 2026)
note: An inner main-belt asteroid drifts about 30 pixels in 3 hours.

label: Slow asteroid De Sitter (Aug 2025)
note: This asteroid is near its turning point in the sky, so it barely moves: over about 10 hours on 16–17 Aug 2025 it shifts less than a pixel. Compare it with Abundantia, which races across the field in a similar time.

label: Quiet deep field (COSMOS)
note: A famous deep-survey field with about 200 SPHEREx frames. Good for spectra and for seeing what 'nothing changed' looks like.

label: SPHEREx deep field at the North Ecliptic Pole (18 months)
note: SPHEREx photographs this spot almost every day: about 29,000 images. We show one combined image for each of 120 days spread over 18 months.
